# Psalm 122 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A song for the journey to Jerusalem. By David. I was so happy when they said to me, 'Let's go to the LORD's house!'

**2** And now we're actually standing here inside your gates, Jerusalem!

**3** Jerusalem — a city built solid and compact,

**4** where all the tribes come together — the LORD's tribes — to fulfill Israel's duty of praising the LORD's name.

**5** That's where the thrones of justice stand — the thrones of David's royal dynasty.

**6** Pray for Jerusalem's peace! May those who love you thrive!

**7** May there be peace inside your walls and prosperity in your homes!

**8** For the sake of my family and friends, I say, 'Peace to you!'

**9** For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will work for your good.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **122:6**: 'Pray for the peace of Jerusalem' — one of the most quoted lines in all the Psalms. The Hebrew wordplay is untranslatable: sha'alu shelom Yerushalayim — 'ask for the shalom of the city of shalom.'

— PNEUMA
